CA.name: California
CA.citation: California FTB 2025 Form 540 tax rate schedules list California personal income tax brackets by filing status.
CA.notes: Base rate schedule only; 1% Mental Health Services Tax over $1,000,000 not modeled (MVP estimate). HOH brackets are CA-specific (not same as Single); thresholds scaled to match OA 2025 projected indexing. OA does not provide separate HOH thresholds. Verify against FTB 2025 Form 540.

tax_base.citation: California Form 540 instructions list 2025 California standard deduction amounts. California federal-conformity guidance says California does not conform to the federal qualified business income deduction under IRC Section 199A.
tax_base.notes: State-specific Schedule CA adjustments, age/blind extra amounts, exemption credits, and other credits are not modeled. Standard deduction values are OA 2025 projected. Verify against FTB 2025 Form 540. Source_id ca_2025_540_tax_rate_schedules may have more current values.

NY.name: New York
NY.citation: New York 2025 IT-201 instructions and tax tables list marginal tax brackets by filing status.
NY.notes: Marginal brackets only; tax benefit recapture above $107,650 NYAGI not modeled (estimate understates above that).

tax_base.citation: New York 2025 IT-201 instructions list the New York State standard deduction table by filing status.
tax_base.notes: New York modifications, credits, and tax benefit recapture above $107,650 NYAGI are not modeled.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.citation: New Jersey Division of Taxation gross income tax overview says New Jersey has a graduated income tax rate and the tax rate schedules list brackets by filing status.
NJ.notes: Gross income tax approximation only; pension exclusions, medical deductions, credits, and other New Jersey-specific deductions are not modeled.

tax_base.citation: New Jersey gross income tax overview says filers at or below the annual filing-status income thresholds pay no tax, and lists a $1,000 taxpayer exemption plus a $1,000 spouse/civil union partner exemption when not filing separately.
tax_base.notes: The MVP uses federal above-line-deduction-before gross income as a proxy for New Jersey gross income. New Jersey-specific income categories, pension exclusions, medical deductions, property tax deduction, dependent exemptions, age/blind exemptions, credits, and residency allocation are not modeled. Qualifying surviving spouse is modeled as MFJ-equivalent (Rate Schedule II plus two $1,000 exemptions) consistent with its surviving-spouse continuation purpose; the exact NJ QSS personal-exemption count is not authoritatively confirmed.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.citation: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue personal income tax rate page lists the rate as 3.07% from 2004-present.
PA.notes: Pennsylvania class-of-income loss rules, exclusions, deductions, credits, local earned income taxes, and residency allocation are not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue personal income tax overview says Pennsylvania personal income tax is levied at 3.07% against taxable income and taxes eight classes of income. This MVP uses gross income as the PA taxable income proxy.
tax_base.notes: The MVP approximates Pennsylvania taxable income as federal above-line-deduction-before gross income. Pennsylvania class-of-income loss rules, deductions, exclusions, credits, and local income taxes are not modeled.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.citation: Oregon Department of Revenue 2025 Form OR-40 instructions, Publication OR-17, and estimated tax instructions list Oregon tax rate charts, standard deductions, and the federal tax liability subtraction AGI phaseout table.
OR.notes: Full-year resident state income tax approximation only; Oregon additions/subtractions, itemized deductions, exemption credits, kicker, other credits, local taxes, and resident/source allocation are not modeled.

federal_tax_subtraction.citation: Oregon 2025 Form OR-40 instructions Table 4 lists maximum federal tax liability subtraction limits by filing status and federal AGI range.
federal_tax_subtraction.notes: The MVP applies the table to federal AGI at cent precision; official instructions round return entries to whole dollars and define each phaseout range as at least the lower bound but less than the upper bound.

tax_base.citation: Oregon Publication OR-17 lists 2025 standard deductions by filing status, and Form OR-40 instructions line 10 lists the federal tax liability subtraction and AGI phaseout table.
tax_base.notes: Uses federal AGI minus Oregon standard deduction and modeled federal tax liability subtraction. Oregon-specific additions/subtractions, itemized deductions, and credits are not modeled.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.citation: Illinois Department of Revenue 2025 individual income tax instructions state the Illinois income tax rate is 4.95%.

tax_base.citation: Illinois 2025 IL-1040 exemption instructions list the $2,850 exemption allowance and deny the exemption allowance above $250,000 federal AGI for non-joint filers or $500,000 for joint filers.
tax_base.notes: Illinois additions, subtractions such as federally-taxed retirement income, credits, and exact exemption count beyond filing status are not modeled.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.citation: Colorado Individual Income Tax Guide lists the 2025 Colorado income tax rate as 4.4%.

tax_base.citation: Colorado Individual Income Tax Guide states Colorado income tax is based on federal taxable income and describes a qualified business income deduction addback that may apply.
tax_base.notes: Colorado starts from federal taxable income which is post-QBI deduction. No separate QBI addback needed for the base computation. Colorado additions/subtractions are otherwise not modeled.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.citation: Georgia 2025 IT-511 booklet states the 2025 income tax rate is 5.19%.

tax_base.citation: Georgia 2025 IT-511 booklet lists the 2025 standard deduction by filing status.
tax_base.notes: Georgia retirement income exclusion, additions, subtractions, and credits are not modeled.

FL.name: Florida
FL.citation: Florida Department of Revenue FAQ states Florida does not impose a personal income tax.

WA.name: Washington
WA.citation: Washington Department of Revenue states Washington does not have an individual income tax.

capital_gains_excise.citation: Washington Department of Revenue capital gains guidance states the 2025 standard deduction is $278,000 and the tax applies to long-term capital assets; DOR's tiered-rate special notice states tax year 2025 taxable Washington capital gains are taxed at 7% on the first $1,000,000 and 9.9% above $1,000,000.
capital_gains_excise.notes: Washington capital gains tax is an excise tax, not an income tax. Real estate, retirement accounts, and certain business assets are exempt; crypto is modeled as a non-exempt long-term capital asset when long-term. Residency and Washington allocation are assumed in-state. The $1,000,000 tier is applied to taxable Washington capital gains after the standard deduction, matching the DOR special notice phrasing.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.citation: Nevada Department of Taxation Tax Notes states Nevada does not impose an individual income tax.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.citation: Alaska Department of Revenue states Alaska does not impose a personal income tax.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.citation: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration confirms the Interest and Dividends Tax was fully repealed effective January 1, 2025, per HB 2 (2023 session).
NH.notes: New Hampshire historically taxed interest and dividend income under RSA 77. The tax rate was phased down from 5% to 3% (2023), 2% (2024), and fully repealed effective 2025-01-01. For tax year 2025+, NH imposes no personal income tax.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.citation: South Dakota Department of Revenue states South Dakota does not have an individual income tax.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.citation: Tennessee Department of Revenue confirms the Hall Income Tax on interest and dividends was fully repealed effective January 1, 2021.
TN.notes: Tennessee's Hall Income Tax (on interest and dividend income) was phased out per Public Chapter 3 (2016) and fully repealed effective 2021-01-01. For tax year 2021+, Tennessee imposes no state income tax.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.citation: Wyoming Department of Revenue states Wyoming does not have an individual income tax.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.citation: Arizona Department of Revenue confirms the 2025 individual income tax rate is a flat 2.5 percent.
AZ.notes: Arizona conforms to federal standard deduction; state-specific additions, subtractions, and the 33% charitable deduction increase are not modeled.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.citation: Idaho Tax Commission confirms the 2025 individual income tax rate is 5.3 percent per HB 40 (2025), retroactive to January 1, 2025.
ID.notes: Idaho rate reduced from 5.695% to 5.3% by HB 40 (signed March 2025). Idaho conforms to federal standard deduction. Idaho-specific adjustments (Form 39R) and grocery credit are not modeled.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.citation: Indiana Department of Revenue states the 2025 adjusted gross income tax rate is 3.00 percent.

tax_base.notes: Indiana taxes federal AGI with no standard deduction. Personal exemptions ($1,000 per person, $1,500 per dependent) and county income taxes (0.5%-3%) are not modeled.

IN.notes: Indiana rate is phasing down: 3.15% (2023), 3.05% (2024/2025 per OpenAccountants audit), scheduled 2.95% (2026). County income taxes are not included.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.citation: Iowa Department of Revenue confirms the 2025 individual income tax rate is a flat 3.8 percent, consolidated from prior progressive brackets.
IA.notes: Iowa adopted a flat rate for 2025 (previously progressive). Iowa now uses federal standard/itemized deductions. Personal exemption credits ($40/$80) and Iowa-specific modifications are not modeled.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.citation: Kentucky Department of Revenue announces the 2025 individual income tax rate is 4.0 percent with a standard deduction of $3,270.

tax_base.citation: Kentucky DOR 2025 standard deduction is $3,270, the same for all filing statuses.
tax_base.notes: Kentucky uses a flat standard deduction regardless of filing status. Rate scheduled to drop to 3.5% in 2026 per revenue trigger.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.citation: Louisiana Department of Revenue confirms the 2025 individual income tax rate is a flat 3.0 percent per Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session.

tax_base.citation: Louisiana RIB No. 25-012 states the 2025 standard deduction is $12,500 (single/MFS) and $25,000 (MFJ/HOH/QSS).
tax_base.notes: Louisiana converted from progressive (2/4/6%) to flat 3% effective 2025. Prior personal exemptions and credits repealed. Inflation adjustment begins 2026.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.citation: Michigan Treasury confirms the 2025 individual income tax rate is 4.25 percent.

tax_base.citation: Michigan personal exemption for 2025 is $5,800 per person.
tax_base.notes: Michigan has no standard deduction; the personal exemption ($5,800 per person) is modeled here as the standard deduction equivalent. Dependent exemptions are not included.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.citation: Mississippi Department of Revenue states the 2025 individual income tax rate is 4.4 percent on taxable income above $10,000.

tax_base.citation: Mississippi standard deduction (single $2,300/MFJ $4,600/HOH $3,400) plus personal exemption (single $6,000/MFJ $12,000) combined.
tax_base.notes: Standard deduction includes personal exemption amount. Dependent exemptions ($1,500 each) are not included. Mississippi uses its own independent income computation, not starting from federal AGI or federal taxable income. Mississippi is phasing out its income tax entirely under the Build-Up Mississippi Act.

MS.notes: Mississippi 4.4% rate applies only to taxable income above $10,000 ($10,000 zero bracket). Rate reduced from 4.7% (2024). Income tax being phased out under the Build-Up Mississippi Act (HB 531). Mississippi uses its own independent income computation, not starting from federal AGI or federal taxable income.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.citation: North Carolina Department of Revenue states the 2025 individual income tax rate is 4.25 percent.

tax_base.citation: NCDOR states the 2025 NC standard deduction is $12,750 (single/MFS), $25,500 (MFJ/QSS), and $19,125 (HOH).
tax_base.notes: NC has fixed-date IRC conformity (Jan 1, 2023). NC standard deduction is set by the General Assembly, not tied to federal amounts. Rate reduced from 4.5% (2024), scheduled to drop to 3.99% (2026).

UT.name: Utah
UT.citation: Utah State Tax Commission confirms the 2025 individual income tax rate is 4.5 percent per HB 106 (2025), retroactive to January 1, 2025.
UT.notes: Utah rate reduced from 4.55% to 4.5% by HB 106 (signed May 2025). Utah uses a taxpayer tax credit (6% of federal deductions + state exemptions, phasing out at higher incomes) instead of a standard deduction; this credit is not modeled. Tax approximated as flat rate on federal taxable income.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.citation: Massachusetts Department of Revenue states the 2025 Part B income tax rate is 5 percent, plus a 4 percent surtax on taxable income exceeding $1,083,150.

surtax.citation: Massachusetts voters approved a 4% surtax on annual taxable income exceeding $1,000,000 (indexed for inflation; 2025 threshold: $1,083,150).

tax_base.citation: Massachusetts personal exemption for 2025 is $4,400 (single), $8,800 (MFJ), $6,800 (HOH).
tax_base.notes: Massachusetts has no standard deduction; personal exemptions modeled as standard deduction equivalent. Dependent exemptions ($1,000 each) not included. MA Part A income (12% rate on certain interest/dividends) and Part C (5% on long-term capital gains) are not modeled; all income taxed at Part B rate.

TX.name: Texas
TX.citation: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts states Texas has no state income tax, constitutionally prohibited by Article VIII Section 24-a.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.citation: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration 2025 Form AR1000F instructions list Arkansas individual income tax rate schedules.
AR.notes: Act 1 of the 2024 Second Extraordinary Session reduced top rate from 4.4% to 3.9% effective 2025. Brackets indexed annually. Low-bracket benefit phase-out above $94,700 (effectively flat 3.9% above $100,001) not modeled. $29 personal tax credit per filer/dependent not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Arkansas 2025 standard deduction is $2,410 (single/MFS/HOH) or $4,820 (MFJ/QSS).
tax_base.notes: Arkansas-specific modifications to federal AGI, itemized deduction option, and $29 personal tax credit are not modeled.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.citation: Delaware Division of Revenue 2025 personal income tax forms and instructions list the Delaware tax rate schedule.
DE.notes: Delaware personal exemption credit ($110 per exemption, enhanced $330 for income $18,000-$36,000) not modeled. Delaware-specific modifications and itemized deductions not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Delaware 2025 standard deduction is $3,250 (single/MFS/HOH) or $6,500 (MFJ/QSS).
tax_base.notes: Additional $2,500 deduction for age 65+/blind not modeled. Personal exemption credit ($110/exemption) not modeled.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.citation: Hawaii Department of Taxation 2025 individual income tax rate schedules list Hawaii tax brackets by filing status per Act 46, SLH 2024.
HI.notes: Act 46 (2024) widened bracket thresholds effective 2025. Personal exemption ($1,144) combined into standard deduction. Hawaii modifications to federal AGI, credits, and refundable food/excise tax credit not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Hawaii 2025 standard deduction ($4,400 S/$8,800 MFJ/$6,424 HOH) plus personal exemption ($1,144 per person) combined.
tax_base.notes: Combined standard deduction + personal exemption for primary filer(s). Dependent exemptions ($1,144 each) not included. QSS uses MFJ standard deduction + one personal exemption.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.citation: Kansas Department of Revenue 2025 income tax booklet lists Kansas tax rate schedules and deduction amounts per Senate Bill 1.
KS.notes: SB 1 consolidated three brackets into two and reduced rates effective 2025. Personal exemption ($9,160 per filer) combined into standard deduction. Dependent exemptions ($2,320 each) not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Kansas 2025 standard deduction ($3,605 S/$8,240 MFJ/$4,120 MFS/$6,180 HOH) plus personal exemption ($9,160 per filer, $18,320 MFJ) combined.
tax_base.notes: Combined standard deduction + personal exemption for primary filer(s). Dependent exemptions ($2,320 each) not included. Kansas-specific Schedule S modifications not modeled.

ME.name: Maine
ME.citation: Maine Revenue Services 2025 individual income tax rate schedule lists marginal brackets by filing status.
ME.notes: Personal exemption ($5,150) combined into standard deduction. Standard deduction and personal exemption phase out at high income (not modeled). Dependent exemptions not included. Maine-specific modifications, credits, and property tax fairness credit not modeled. A 9.15% high-income surcharge bracket above the OpenAccountants threshold is included.

tax_base.citation: Maine 2025 standard deduction ($15,000 S/MFS, $30,000 MFJ, $22,500 HOH) plus personal exemption ($5,150 per person) combined.
tax_base.notes: Combined standard deduction + personal exemption for primary filer(s). Phaseout above $100,000 (S) / $200,000 (MFJ) not modeled. Dependent exemptions not included.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.citation: Maryland Comptroller 2025 tax alert lists new state income tax brackets and deduction changes effective for tax years beginning after 12/31/2024.
MD.notes: Two new high-income brackets (6.25% and 6.50%) added for 2025. Personal exemption ($3,200) combined into standard deduction. County income tax (2.25%-3.3%), 2% capital gains surtax above $350K FAGI, and itemized deduction phaseout not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Maryland 2025 standard deduction ($3,350 S/MFS, $6,700 MFJ/HOH/QSS) plus personal exemption ($3,200 per person) combined.
tax_base.notes: Combined standard deduction + personal exemption for primary filer(s). Dependent exemptions ($3,200 each) not included. County income tax adds 2.25%-3.3% and is not modeled.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.citation: Missouri Department of Revenue 2025 tax year changes list Missouri individual income tax brackets indexed for inflation.
MO.notes: Missouri conforms to federal standard deduction. Brackets include a $0-$1,313 zero bracket. Personal exemptions were eliminated. Missouri-specific modifications not modeled.

MT.name: Montana
MT.citation: Montana Department of Revenue 2025 tax rates and deductions list Montana individual income tax brackets per SB 121 (2023).
MT.notes: Montana starts from federal taxable income (federal standard deduction already included). SB 121 (2023) established two-bracket system, reduced top rate from 6.5% to 5.9% effective TY 2024. Brackets indexed annually. Montana-specific additions/subtractions not modeled.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.citation: Nebraska Department of Revenue 2025 individual income tax booklet lists Nebraska tax rate schedules and standard deduction amounts per LB 754 (2023) phased reduction.
NE.notes: LB 754 (2023) phased rate reduction; 2025 top rate 5.20% (from 5.84%). Brackets indexed annually. Personal exemption credit ($157/exemption) not modeled. Nebraska-specific modifications and credits not modeled.

tax_base.citation: Nebraska 2025 standard deduction is $8,600 (single/MFS), $17,200 (MFJ/QSS), $12,600 (HOH).
tax_base.notes: Personal exemption credit ($157 per exemption) is a non-refundable credit against tax, not a deduction. Not modeled.

ND.notes: ND 2025 per HB 1158; 0% bracket exempts first $48,475 single / $96,950 MFJ. Very low rates.

NM.notes: NM 2025 brackets per HB 252; HoH uses MFJ schedule. Dependent deductions and low/middle-income exemption not modeled.

OH.notes: OH 2025; no standard deduction. Personal exemption modeled at >$80k MAGI tier ($1,900/person); stepped exemption ($2,350/$2,100/$1,900 by MAGI) and joint filing credit not modeled. Uniform brackets.

OK.notes: OK 2025; brackets not indexed for inflation. Standard deduction ($6,350/$12,700/$9,350) + personal exemption ($1,000/person) combined. HoH uses single brackets.

RI.notes: RI 2025; uniform brackets. Standard deduction ($10,900/$21,800/$16,350) + personal exemption ($5,100/person) combined; phaseout above $254,250 MAGI not modeled.

SC.notes: SC 2025; uniform brackets, 0% on first $3,560. Uses federal taxable income. Dependent exemption ($4,930/dependent) not modeled. Major reform in 2026 (H.4216).

VA.notes: VA 2025; uniform brackets with very low thresholds. Standard deduction ($8,750/$17,500) + personal exemption ($930/person) combined; standard deduction phaseout above $50k single / $75k MFJ NOT modeledoverstates deduction for high earners.

VT.notes: VT 2025; indexed brackets. Vermont starts from federal taxable income, so federal deductions are already reflected and no separate state standard deduction is modeled.

WV.notes: WV 2025 per SB 2033; uniform brackets. No standard deduction; personal exemption ($2,000/person) modeled as standard_deduction.

AL.notes: AL 2025; 3 brackets (2%/4%/5%). Standard deduction ($3,000/$8,500) + personal exemption ($1,500/$3,000) combined; standard deduction phaseout NOT modeled. Federal tax subtraction with no cap. Dependent exemption ($1,000 or $300 by income) not modeled.

CT.notes: CT 2025; 7 brackets (2%-6.99%). No standard deduction. Personal exemptions ($15,000/$24,000) are tax credits, NOT modeled. Benefit recapture (Tables C/D) NOT modeled--understates tax for high earners.

DC.notes: DC 2025; 7 brackets (4%-10.75%), uniform. Standard deduction $15,000/$30,000. Personal exemptions eliminated for 2025.

MN.notes: MN 2025; 4 brackets (5.35%-9.85%), indexed. Standard deduction $14,950/$29,900. 1% net investment income surtax on >$1M NOT modeled (applies to investment income only, not wage income). Dependent exemption ($5,200/dependent) not modeled. MN DOR starts the income tax computation from federal taxable income; existing standard deduction field is retained for state-specific adjustments pending deeper modeling.

WI.notes: WI 2025; 4 brackets (3.50%-7.65%). Standard deduction ($13,560/$25,110) + personal exemption ($700/person) combined; sliding-scale standard deduction phaseout NOT modeled--overstates deduction for higher earners.
